title: Collectives: poll NCCL async errors + propagate failures to scheduler (flags + defaults)
author: Hiro Tanaka
description:
Context: In recent TP hang incidents we see ranks stuck in a collective with no forward progress, but the scheduler continues to assign work because the collective executor never reports an error (async NCCL errors can remain latent until the next NCCL API call). This PR adds periodic async error polling for NCCL communicators and a single, consistent propagation path into the runtime scheduler so TP groups can be marked failed quickly (and stop accepting work) instead of silently stalling.

What changed: (1) Add an AsyncErrorMonitor that periodically polls ncclCommGetAsyncError() for active TP communicators (and optionally cudaGetLastError() for the collective stream) on a timer, without requiring a new collective launch. (2) When an async error is observed, translate it into a structured RuntimeError (category=CollectiveAsyncError) and immediately notify the scheduler via TpGroupEvent::CollectiveFailure, including tp_group_id, rank, communicator_id, and nccl_error string. (3) Ensure the collective executor unblocks any waiters and fails outstanding requests with a clear error instead of waiting indefinitely for a barrier/collective completion that will never happen. (4) Add config flags + deployment defaults for enabling the monitor and controlling polling interval.

Config flags: - runtime.collectives.async_error_check_enabled (bool): default=true when tp_world_size>1 (Hosted/Dedicated), default=false in Private unless explicitly enabled (to avoid surprising behavior in air-gapped / older driver environments). - runtime.collectives.async_error_check_interval_ms (int): default=250 (chosen to detect stalls quickly without measurable overhead in our microbench). - runtime.collectives.async_error_fail_fast (bool): default=true; when false we only emit logs/metrics but do not fail the group (intended for debugging).

Metrics/logs: - runtime_collectives_async_error_total{model,region,tp_world_size,nccl_error} - runtime_collectives_async_error_last_seen_seconds (gauge) - Structured log "collective_async_error" includes tp_group_id/rank/comm_id/sequence_id and links to a short remediation hint.

Testing: - Added unit tests with a fake NCCL communicator that flips into an async error state and verifies propagation to the scheduler. - Added a GPU integration test (guarded) that injects a forced NCCL error (via test-only hook) and asserts we fail the in-flight request within 2*interval_ms. - Ran tp-hang repro harness scenario "rank_delay_then_cancel" locally (A100 8x) to verify we surface the error and the scheduler stops routing new work to that TP group.

Rollout notes: This PR only surfaces failures earlier + more deterministically. Quarantine/restart policy is handled in follow-up PRs (watchdog/quarantine). For runtime-1.19 hotfix, the defaults are conservative for Private and enabled by default for Hosted/Dedicated TP>1.

Checklist: - [x] Linked Linear issue (ENG-2406) - [x] Added metrics + structured logs - [x] Added unit + integration coverage - [x] Documented flags + defaults (inline + config docs) - [x] Confirmed no perf regression in microbench (see notes below)

Perf notes: Polling is O(active_comms) once per interval and does not touch the hot path of collective launches. Microbench (continuous batching, TP=8, seq_len mix 128/512) shows <0.2% throughput variance vs baseline (within noise).

review_conversation: Sofia Ivanova: Can we guarantee we don't deadlock when failing outstanding requests that are mid-barrier? Specifically, if one rank surfaces async error and others are still blocked on a scheduler barrier, do we release them deterministically?

Hiro Tanaka (author): Yes. The handler path calls TpGroup::FailAllInflight("CollectiveAsyncError") which (a) marks the group as Failed, (b) completes all request promises with error, and (c) broadcasts a cancel token to all barrier participants. For ranks still running, they will observe the cancel token on the next scheduler tick and stop enqueuing new collectives. This is the same completion path we use for explicit request cancellations; added a test that the barrier waiters unblock within one tick.
Rafael Mendes: Default enablement in Private worries me; we have customers with older NCCL/driver stacks. Can we default it off in Private until we validate on the private installer matrix?

Hiro Tanaka (author): Agreed. Updated defaults: Hosted/Dedicated enable when tp_world_size>1; Private default=false (explicit opt-in). Added a log line when TP>1 but monitor disabled to reduce confusion during triage.
Grace Kim: What is the steady-state overhead of polling ncclCommGetAsyncError every 250ms across many active comms? Also, do we need jitter to avoid synchronized polling across processes?

Hiro Tanaka (author): Overhead is minimal (single NCCL call per comm per interval). We only register comms that are "active" (used within last 30s) and de-register on teardown. Added +/-10% jitter per process to reduce alignment (see async_error_monitor.cc). Also added a perf note in the PR body; ran microbench and didn't see regression beyond noise.
Noah Patel: Failure propagation: we should ensure error reason is preserved up to the API layer for customer troubleshooting. Are we currently collapsing this into a generic 500?

Hiro Tanaka (author): Good catch. Updated error mapping to set error_code=RUNTIME_COLLECTIVE_ASYNC_ERROR and include nccl_error + tp_group_id in the internal error details; API layer still returns 5xx but logs/trace include the structured event. Follow-up PR will improve user-facing messaging in Dedicated console.
Omar El-Sayed: Metric cardinality: nccl_error label could explode if we include full strings. Can we label by enum and log the string?
Hiro Tanaka (author): Updated to label by normalized enum (e.g., "ncclUnhandledCudaError") and include full message only in logs. Pushed fix in last commit.
